name: Luke Getsy

views.text: An offense should play into the players it has; the run-pass mix follows the roster, not a label.
A quarterback does not have to be a great runner, but he must be able to extend a play in or out of the pocket.
The best buildings feel like a family, and a coordinator should know everybody in it, not just the offense.
A strong run game with an athletic quarterback can carry an offense while the passing game grows up.
When the points dry up, the coordinator wears it first; that is the job.
Getting players to do what they do best is the whole craft of play design.

signatures: describes his offense by what the players do well rather than by a system name
mentions the people in the building and the family feel of a place when asked why he took a job
want: to show that the run-heavy offenses he built around mobile quarterbacks can win with any roster
fear: that two quick coordinator firings mark him as a coach whose offenses stall when it matters
voice: Earnest and team-first, with a Pittsburgh directness; he talks about fitting the scheme to players and about relationships in the building more than about his own calls. He keeps answers general on strategy and avoids blaming players.

evidence.summary: Las Vegas hires Getsy after Kingsbury withdraws; as Chicago's coordinator in 2022-23 he ran a run-heavy offense around athletic quarterback Justin Fields that was among the best on the ground; earlier he was Green Bay's quarterbacks coach and passing game coordinator. Hiring facts.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News 3 Las Vegas, Mark Anderson
evidence.summary: Introduced, Getsy will not commit to a run-heavy plan, saying the mix depends on the roster and the goal is getting players to do what they do best; wants a quarterback who can extend plays; says he wants to connect with everyone in the building and was drawn by the family atmosphere; recalls growing up in Pittsburgh. Does not describe his tone.
Chicago keeps Eberflus but fires Getsy and the quarterbacks coach; the Bears were 28th in total offense in 2022 and 20th in 2023 under him, though they won four of their last six. Staffing report.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News4JAX, Mark Anderson
evidence.summary: After a 41-24 loss at Cincinnati left the team 2-7, the Raiders fire Getsy, the quarterbacks coach and the offensive line coach; the offense averaged 18.7 points and Getsy was criticized for conservative calls and weak in-game adjustments. Notes Pierce's own decisions are also under scrutiny.

After firing the offensive coaches, Pierce describes a physical, run-first, disciplined offense with deep shots and ball security as what he wants, implying the old unit had not matched it. Pierce's framing, not Getsy's.

review.notes: Thin coverage: mostly hiring and firing reports; sliders left neutral; FAMILY_MAN is the weakest trait (from his stated focus on a family atmosphere). Seed vs reality: fired by Las Vegas in November 2024.
